agenda_items.title: Embodied Agency — Intelligence Exists Because It Can Act and Observe Consequences
agenda_items.intent_description: Define embodied agency as the architectural principle that intelligence exists because it can act and observe consequences — not because it can talk. Nexus agents gain embodiment through OpenCode integration: they read the actual repo, edit real files, run compilers and tests, observe results, and retry. The model describes changes (representational) is replaced with the model acts inside reality (operational). This is the foundation for organizational intelligence: the system learns from actual outcomes, not prompt feedback.
requirements: Agency through action and consequence observation
OpenCode as embodiment layer — reads/writes real filesystem
Organizational intelligence from actual outcomes, not prompt feedback
Act > describe — operational AI replaces representational AI
System learns from environment feedback, not human evaluation

agenda_items.title: Nexus as Artificial Organization — Event Brain + Hands + Reasoning Cortex + Reality + Physics Laws
agenda_items.intent_description: Define Nexus's architecture as an artificial organization: Nexus = Event Brain (event substrate + projections), OpenCode = Hands (filesystem manipulation), Ollama/Qwen = Reasoning Cortex (LLM-based generation), Filesystem/Compiler = Reality (the ground truth of what works), Tests = Physics Laws (the invariant verifier). This makes Nexus an 'artificial organization' rather than a tool — it coordinates cognitive labor the way an organization coordinates human labor, with defined roles, authority, and accountability.
requirements: Event Brain: event substrate coordinates all cognition
Hands: OpenCode manifests actions as filesystem changes
Reasoning Cortex: LLMs generate plans and solutions
Reality: filesystem and compiler as ground truth
Physics Laws: tests as invariant verifiers
Organization model replaces tool model

agenda_items.title: Three-Layer Agent Economy — Compute (Energy) → Attention (Allocation) → Trust (Credit)
agenda_items.intent_description: Define the three-layer economy that emerges in mature agent systems: (1) Resource Economy — tokens, GPU time, API calls, disk IO, execution slots (equivalent to fuel/energy). (2) Attention Economy — decision attention as the scarce resource: which task runs first, which proposal gets reasoning time, which agent gets context allocation. Schedulers quietly become central banks. (3) Trust Economy — agents earn trust operationally through reliability and accuracy. Trust reduces oversight cost. Trusted agents consume fewer approvals. All three layers must exist for stable institutional growth.
requirements: Three layers: Resource (energy), Attention (allocation), Trust (credit)
Tokens = fuel, not money
Schedulers = central banks of attention economy
Trust reduces approval overhead — credit for agents
All three layers must exist for stable agent society

agenda_items.title: Institutional Economy — Legitimacy as the Ultimate Currency in Agent Systems
agenda_items.intent_description: Recognize that once compute, tokens, trust, and attention economies exist, legitimacy becomes the ultimate currency. No matter how clever agents are, if their proposals, actions, and optimizations aren't recognized by the governance structure, they are effectively invisible. Legitimacy determines whether a proposed workflow, ontology change, or agent decision actually matters. It is the acceptance layer that gates authority. The event kernel, civil service, and token economy all become tools to enforce and calibrate legitimacy.
requirements: Legitimacy = acceptance layer → gates authority
Tokens = enables action, Compute = enables execution, Trust = enables autonomy
Legitimacy = enables authority
Event kernel, civil service, token economy enforce legitimacy
Legitimacy infrastructure: mechanisms, approvals, flows that make authority operational
